claims.text: What the strip looks like A short QT that does not change normally with heart rate, peaked T waves (especially precordial) and short or absent ST segments.
claims.quote: Short QT interval Lack of normal changes in QT interval with heart rate Peaked T waves, particularly in precordial leads Short, or absent, ST segments

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) QTc: < 330 ms in men or < 340 ms in women is diagnostic of short QT syndrome
claims.quote: QTc intervals < 330 ms in males or < 340 ms in females should be considered diagnostic of SQTS

claims.text: QTc < 360 ms (men) or < 370 ms (women): diagnostic only with symptoms or family history
claims.quote: QTc intervals < 360 ms in males or < 370 ms in females should only be considered diagnostic of SQTS when supported by symptoms or family history

claims.text: QT with rate: fixed — stays constant across heart rates, so at fast rates the QTc can look “pseudonormal”
claims.quote: Patients with SQTS demonstrate fixed QT intervals which remain constant over a range of heart rates At fast heart rates, the calculated QTc may appear normal (= ”pseudonormal” QTc)
claims.locator: Lack of normal changes in QT with heart rate

claims.text: T waves: peaked, especially in the precordial leads
claims.quote: Peaked T waves, particularly in precordial leads

claims.text: Rhythm: paroxysmal atrial or ventricular fibrillation
claims.quote: Paroxysmal episodes of atrial or ventricular fibrillation

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Hypercalcemia: short QT and short ST segment
claims.quote: Hypercalcemia: Short QT, short ST segment

claims.text: Digoxin effect: “scooped” ST depression and a short QT
claims.quote: Effect: "Scooped" / "Salvador Dalí mustache" ST depression, short QT
claims.locator: 12. Important "Can't-Miss" Patterns, Digoxin Effect vs. Toxicity

claims.text: Short QT syndrome: an inherited channelopathy on the same spectrum as long QT, Brugada and CPVT
claims.quote: Genetically-inherited cardiac channelopathy, on the same spectrum as other familial arrhythmogenic diseases such as Long QT syndrome (LQTS), Brugada Syndrome, and Catecholamine Polymorphic Ventricular Tachycardia (CPVT)

claims.text: Mechanism (genotypes 1–3): gain-of-function potassium channel mutations → more K⁺ efflux → faster repolarization → QT < 320 ms
claims.quote: SQTS genotypes 1-3 are produced by a gain-of-function mutation in myocardial potassium channels (the opposite to LQTS), with increased potassium efflux during various stages of the action potential leading to more rapid atrial and ventricular repolarisation with marked shortening of the QT interval (<320 ms).

claims.text: Why it causes arrhythmias: very short atrial and ventricular refractory periods plus uneven repolarization across the wall favor re-entry
claims.quote: Extremely short atrial and ventricular refractory periods (manifest on the ECG as a short QT interval) Transmural dispersion of repolarisation, i.e., the different layers of the myocardium (endocardium, epicardium and the mid-myocardial ‘M-cells’) repolarise at different rates Both these repolarisation abnormalities convey an increased susceptibility to re-entrant atrial and ventricular arrhythmias.

claims.text: Who: typically young and healthy with structurally normal hearts; median age at presentation 30 years
claims.quote: Patients are typically young and healthy, with no structural heart abnormalities; age at first presentation ranges from a few months to the sixth decade of life (median age = 30 years)

claims.text: Symptoms Cardiac arrest is the most common first presentation (one-third); others present with palpitations or syncope from rapid AF or self-terminating ventricular arrhythmias
claims.quote: The most common initial presenting symptom is cardiac arrest (in one-third of cases); other patients may present with palpitations or syncope due to rapid atrial fibrillation or self-terminating ventricular arrhythmias

claims.text: Treatment Short QT syndrome: an ICD is the only effective treatment
claims.quote: At present, the only effective treatment is implantation of an ICD

claims.text: Quinidine is the drug of choice (prolongs the QT and ventricular refractory period)
claims.quote: Quinidine is currently the agent of choice, having been shown in SQTS 1 patients to markedly prolong both the QT interval and ventricular refractory period

notes.issue: Quote supported only pseudonormal QTc at fast rates, not "fixed".
